A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MMControl research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison. v3 retains Appendices A–B and adds C–D.

before.justification: v1 reports original generation experiments, quantitative baseline comparisons, qualitative control studies, human evaluation, and audio-quality measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical results and adds quantitative pose evaluation, component and guidance-scaling ablations, and an AVControl comparison.

M1.justification: The MMCU inputs and masks, dual-stream bypass architecture, modality-specific guidance, and two-stage inference remain unchanged in Section 3. The new ablation variants test the existing method rather than revise the proposed model.

E1.justification: Both versions train on 30,000 Hallo3 samples and cover reference-image/audio, depth, and pose conditioning. Pose control already appears in v1 Figure 6. Its new quantitative evaluation and the added appendix experiments do not introduce a new dataset, domain, or task.

E2.justification: v3 adds AVControl as a comparator for depth and pose control in Table S5. Existing comparator sets are retained; Text2Video-Zero, ControlVideo, and VACE already participated in v1's qualitative pose comparison.

E3.justification: v3 extends evaluation with quantitative pose MAE and temporal consistency, component comparisons on 90 paired samples, an AVControl comparison on 60 samples, and guidance sweeps over 0.5, 1.0, and 1.3. The original training settings, 200-sample audio/depth benchmarks, human-study design, and 150-case audio evaluation remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained qualitative guidance study in Figure 7, Appendix C adds substantial quantitative validation. Table S3 tests masks, projector initialization, unified attention, removal of each bypass branch, and added cross-attention across audio/depth/pose tasks. Table S4 adds guidance-strength sensitivity analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The new 90- and 60-sample counts describe evaluation samples, not repeated runs or uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Tables 1, 2, S1, and S2 retain their values. Substantial new results include pose MAE ×100 of 3.07 versus VACE's 3.29 in Table 3, component and guidance results in Tables S3–S4, and AVControl comparisons in Table S5: depth MAE 11.49 versus MMControl's 4.52 and pose MAE 7.57 versus 3.07. These are newly reported comparisons, not improvements over v1 under matched settings.

T1.justification: Equations 1–5 retain the same task mapping, conditional representations, masks, projection, and residual guidance formulation. No new theorem, proof, derivation, or substantive mathematical revision appears.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction narrow broad references to scene layout and diverse control scenarios to depth-guided scene structure and reference/depth/pose conditioning. The central MMCU, dual-stream bypass, guidance-scaling, and state-of-the-art claims remain.

C2.justification: Appendix C adds interpretations connecting component removals to synchronization, speaker similarity, and structural errors. Appendix D explains the loudness-versus-timbre distinction limiting the AVControl comparison and acknowledges its pose-aesthetics advantage. Section 4.3 also qualifies VACE comparisons and separates visual structural evaluation from joint audio-video capability.

D1.justification: Appendix C specifies the six ablation modifications and exact guidance values, including fixing the other scale at 1. These add limited reproducibility information. The original backbone, optimizer, training budget, hardware, preprocessing, and audio-evaluation tools remain unchanged; no new code or data access information appears.

R1.justification: v3 adds references for AVControl and Text2Video-Zero. Appendix D positions AVControl as concurrent work using task-specific IC-LoRA adapters and distinguishes its acoustic control target. The main related-work discussion otherwise retains its existing positioning.

P1.justification: v3 tightens wording throughout the method, experiments, and conclusion while retaining the main section sequence and narrative. It adds a main-text summary of existing human/audio results, expands the appendix outline, and changes citation style and author/header presentation.

P2.justification: The document is comprehensively reformatted with different typography, text width, running headers, and figure/table placement. Four tables are added: Table 3 and Tables S3–S5. The seven existing figures retain their illustrated content but are resized or relocated, with several captions revised.

improvement.justification: v1 lacked component ablations and supported pose control only qualitatively. v3 substantially strengthens evidence for its central contributions through quantitative pose evaluation, component and guidance studies, and a relevant concurrent baseline comparison. Narrower scope statements and more careful comparison language also improve precision. The added studies still lack uncertainty estimates and detailed protocols, but they address important gaps in the original empirical support.
